tldr:
For fixed ordered bounded potential outcomes, nearly deterministic Efron balancing has a proved three-level phase diagram for the causal average \(\tau_N\). With nonzero even signed marks, the first intensity \(\lambda_N=N\varepsilon\) governs a centered compound-Poisson conditional-IPW coordinate and an independent Gaussian marginal-HT coordinate; their finite-table product approximation has error at most \(64(\sqrt\varepsilon+N^{-1/2})\). Growing intensity gives the stated Gaussian normalization, while subcritical rare spikes explain skew compensation and possible nonuniform integrability. When every even outcome is zero, the second intensity \(\kappa_N=N\varepsilon^2\) governs the root-\(N\) law, with dependence through a common Gaussian component. On the exact antisymmetric odd-row subclass, the marginal error vanishes identically and the conditional error has the proved \(N\)-scale compound-Poisson and \(N/\sqrt{\lambda_N}\)-scale Gaussian laws under their stated conditions; at \(\lambda_N\to0\), an explicit table obstructs a universal nondegenerate finer normalization.

An original-record signed compound-Poisson diagnostic is also proved, with \(O(\sqrt\varepsilon+N^{-1/2})\) expected transport error and finite-convolution atomic quantile brackets carrying an explicit Poisson tail charge. Original-record pair squares converge to \(v_N+h_N\) and give uniformly conservative marginal Wald coverage over every shrinking bias envelope on \(\mathcal C_N(v_0)\), with asymptotically exact coverage when \(h_N\to0\). The public variance floor applies only to that coverage class. Conditional-IPW worst-table consistency holds exactly when \(N\varepsilon\to\infty\) over the full bounded class \(\mathcal M_N\); the same records retain uniformly consistent marginal inference.

Exact assignment covariance and independent-pair calibration do not supply a dependent-design transfer uniform over arbitrary shrinking envelopes.
